root_cause.text: In `iomap_read_folio_iter()`, `ctx->cur_folio` is not invalidated when I/O is submitted for less than the full folio size in the absence of an `iomap_folio_state` (`ifs`), causing both the I/O helper and `iomap_read_end()` to concurrently claim ownership of the folio.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that when `1 << inode->i_blkbits` matches the folio size but differs from the I/O granularity, "the condition: `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len) ctx->cur_folio = NULL;` in `iomap_read_folio_iter()` will not invalidate `ctx->cur_folio`, and `iomap_read_end()` will still be called on the folio even though the IO helper owns it". This is resolved in the patch by changing the check to `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len || !ifs) ctx->cur_folio = NULL;`.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit is the fix for the vulnerability. It introduces the check `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len) ctx->cur_folio = NULL;` in `iomap_read_folio_iter()` to invalidate the folio pointer when the IO helper takes ownership of the entire folio. It also adds a check `if (ctx->cur_folio)` before calling `iomap_read_end()` in `iomap_read_folio()`, preventing concurrent ownership claims and invalid folio access.
